items.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And I’ve played John Coltrane tunes and worked with Tom Harrell.

ctx.x: So I wouldn’t think that you’re — I suppose some of the press you’re getting is more that you’re, as Scott says, “Ken has helped to keep the tradition of a small group swing alive” in one of the books. But that’s not all you’re doing.

That’s not all I do and I just hate labels like that. Because as somebody gives you a label, even if they’re well meaning, that’s what you become in everybody’s eyes. Or it becomes a jazz fact if it’s published in the books. I just hate those kind of things. And if you look back through a lot of interviews with older musicians — Duke always hated that too, or Sonny Stitt hated to be called a Charlie Parker imitator. And I hate to even have to justify what I do, but like the last few records, I did this thing with…

Coltrane tune, and they’ve got their eyes closed and they’re thinking Benny Goodman swing. So it’s fine. It’s okay. But I think I tend to bristle any time any label comes up, even if it’s well meaning.
